speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Another Member, Ms Sun Xueling, has also spoken about milk powder in her interviews with the Straits Times and Lianhe Zaobao over the weekend.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The Government is as concerned as Members are about the high price of infant formula.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: We have been monitoring the situation and taking steps to address the concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The Health Promotion Board (HPB) and international organisations, including the World Health Organization (WHO), strongly encourage breastfeeding as it can provide the nutritional needs of infants, with the added benefits of promoting mother-child bonding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Breast milk is the best milk to meet the nutritional needs of infants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: HPB recommends that, where possible, mothers should exclusively breastfeed their babies for the first six months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Between six and 12 months, babies should be given breast milk along with complementary foods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: For children above 12 months of age, cows' milk, as part of a balanced diet, is adequate to meet their nutritional needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Formula milk is not required for children beyond the first year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: We recognise that, in some cases, infants cannot be exclusively breastfed and will need infant formula as a form of supplementation or the main form of their feeding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Hence, we have food regulations which stipulate quality and safety standards for infant formula milk sold in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Singapore's standards are similar to international standards in terms of required essential vitamins and minerals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Some infant formula companies give the impression that their particular brands of milk powder can do more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Without better information, parents should be careful about relying on the claims made by infant formula companies or be misled into using price as a proxy for the quality of the product.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The Government will take steps to address this problem, including referencing the best practices in other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Public awareness is important to support parents in deciding what is best for their children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: HPB, together with healthcare institutions and healthcare professionals, will get the message out, especially to mothers-to-be.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Besides consumer education, the Government will also do more through these few things.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Hospitals play an important role where healthcare professionals provide information and advice to parents, and infants have many first experiences in our hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: All hospitals, both public and private, encourage and support breastfeeding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: They will provide infant formula when needed, for example, if the mother is unable to produce enough milk to meet the baby's needs or for specific medical reason for which the mother should be discouraged from breastfeeding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: For example, when she is on certain medications or on chemotherapy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) will work with industry players to make available more infant formula options in the hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: We will also strongly encourage all hospitals providing maternity services to achieve the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative (BFHI) certification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: All public hospitals offering maternity services are already BFHI-certified today, but private hospitals have yet to come on board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: BFHI-certified hospitals are committed to actively encourage and support breastfeeding targets and are not allowed to enter into sponsorship arrangements with milk powder companies, given the potential for conflicts of interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: We hope private hospitals will see that this is beneficial for their patients and will come on board to support this important initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: CCS will publish its report this week, and more details will be available then.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Should there be any evidence of companies acting in concert to increase prices together, CCS will not hesitate to investigate the anti-competitive behaviour under the Competition Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: In Singapore, the six major manufacturers which supply formula milk have a market presence which is much bigger than the other manufacturers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: This was a point also highlighted by Ms Sun Xueling in her online survey of about 2,500 respondents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The Government will simplify and streamline import requirements, as well as remove unnecessary barriers to entry, in order to bring in more options for parents but, most importantly, without compromising food safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Besides doing all these, at the same time, we should also improve consumer protection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The Government will strengthen restrictions on advertising and labelling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The Sale of Infant Food Ethics Committee, Singapore (SIFECS) Code of Ethics already restricts advertising, marketing and promotion of infant formula for infants below six months in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Nevertheless, HPB is supporting an ongoing review of the SIFECS Code which will include extending its coverage to all infant formula for infants up to 12 months of age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: This will also discourage companies from incurring massive costs on aggressive advertising and marketing activities and passing these costs on to consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: In this regard, ComCare provides assistance to low-income families in financial need, including families raising infants and young children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: They can approach their nearest Social Service Office (SSO) to apply for ComCare Short-to-Medium Term Assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The SSO will assess their needs, and families may receive cash assistance for their basic needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: To conclude, Madam, I would like to reiterate that the Government shares parents' concern about rising prices of formula milk in Singapore and is committed to addressing them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) will also remind businesses to price their products fairly and look into consumer feedback on potential profiteering.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I have a few supplementary questions to ask.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: First of all, would the Senior Minister of State be able to share why is it that milk powder is priced so highly in Singapore, compared with other comparable countries and over time?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The jump is too significant, in my opinion, to be explained by operating cost increases.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Also, milk powder is seen as essential for growing infants since they can only rely on milk.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: And a lot of young parents feel that they are held to ransom, especially for those with special medical needs.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Could that be one of the reasons driving the price increase and, if so, would the Government consider control measures, such as those implemented in countries like China, on top of introducing more competition, so that there is greater pressure to ensure that throughout the supply chain, the pricing is fairer and so that it is more affordable for young parents in Singapore?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In terms of setting a price for special formulas, children who have specific needs for which normal milk formula cannot fulfil, for example, specific allergies or medical conditions, will, therefore, require more expensive formula feeds because of the special formulation required.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It will be quite difficult for us to restrict a particular formula for its price, because there is definitely a research and development expenditure that the company has to incur.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: What we can do is to make sure that we increase the choices that are available and, where necessary, put in the necessary financial support to these families to defray the cost of such formula that they require.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But hopefully, these are a more restricted group of infants.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There is also a big range of milk formula pricing on the shelves today.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Some can go for about $20-plus to $30 for a 900-gramme tin, and others can go up to about $60.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, within this range, parents do have a choice.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And I think this is where education of the parents to allay their anxiety that they are not shortchanging their children by giving them the cheaper option, because the cheaper option, nutritionally, is just as good as the more expensive ones.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And this is where we can introduce the much more robust and healthier competition within the market by removing the information asymmetry.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned changing the import requirements to allow more choice, for other brands being brought into the market.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If there are any changes to, for example, regulations, we will also need a little bit of time to engage vendors so that they have the "go-ahead" to go and bring in some of these new products.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, by end of this year, we hope to be able to finalise some of these changes.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: It is an issue that many of my Clementi residents worry about as well.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: As background, I note the recent CPI report mentioned milk, cheese and eggs under food, but not specifically infant formula.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Milk powder for infants' full cream milk powder and other milk powder, even skimmed milk powder are already included in the CPI basket for this category of food.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For the second question, the report on Household Expenditure Survey 2012-2013 published by the Department of Statistics contains data on average monthly household expenditure by household living arrangements, such as by the age group of the head of the household, the number of children in the family, and the age of the youngest child, as well as by household income group.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, there is some data that we already have.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This data can be used to study and understand the expenditure of different types of households, including households with younger heads of family as well as young children.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But let us also understand that expenditure is very much influenced by consumer choices and consumer behaviour.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Therefore, this is where I go back to the point about educating our parents to understand that expensive does not mean it is better; cheaper does not mean it is worse.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There should be no guilt on the parents' part about buying the cheaper brand of milk.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As long as your child can get used to the milk, or they are not suffering from any allergic reaction to that particular brand of milk, there is no real reason to really pay out more when there is something that is just as good and much cheaper.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is where education needs to play a role to help households rationalise their expenditure.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I was told that it could cost $45 to $105 for two to three days, depending on whether there is tube-feeding needed for kids requiring milk powder for special allergies.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And if the extensive plan from the Senior Minister of State can also look into coordinating with the rest of Government to ensure that the right support is available for needy parents who need expensive formulations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Also, at the community level, there are ways we can help these families as well, outside the schemes from Government.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, most of us would have ComCare funds we can use or even Community Development and Welfare Fund (CDWF) that we can also mobilise for short-term support, while the hospital tries to sort out how they can help these specific children with needs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Pre-term infants who require special formulas are a different category altogether but, fortunately, they are not the bulk of the kind of infants that we have to take care of.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, on a case-by-case basis, we can look at how to assist them.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: While it needs to be verified, I think it is a genuine concern and I hope that the Government can assure us that during this time where the necessary changes are being worked out, that it will continue to monitor very closely to ensure that young parents are not taken advantage of during this period.
